$comment: The context ladder: every level every eval task is run at. Each level gives the agent ONE source of Helix knowledge and nothing else (no AGENTS.md under the MCP or the lint loop), so each one's effect is measured on its own; full repo is everything together. Single source for `pnpm eval:ladder` (what to generate), and Proof (proof.config.mjs). `flags` are eval:generate flags; `explain` is the plain-language tooltip the galleries show next to the level.

levels.label: no help (control)
levels.detail: No Helix guide, no repo — expected to fail
levels.explain: Control group, expected to fail: the agent gets nothing about Helix — no guide, no files, no tools. Helix is not public, so no model has ever seen it and it invents package and prop names. Not a Helix bug: it is the baseline that shows how much every other level helps.

levels.label: llms.txt
levels.explain: Only llms.txt, the short summary of Helix published for AI tools. Tests whether a summary alone is enough to build with Helix.

levels.label: agents-md
levels.explain: Only AGENTS.md, Helix's full guide for coding agents (components, props, tokens, rules) — no repo, no tools.

levels.label: mcp
levels.detail: Only the Helix MCP tools — no guide, no repo
levels.explain: No guide — only the Helix MCP tools: while it works, the agent can look up component contracts, search tokens and check its own code.

levels.label: lint loop
levels.detail: Only its Helix lint problems and type errors, sent back to fix — no guide, no repo
levels.explain: No guide — the agent answers, helix_validate_snippet checks the code (Helix's lint rules plus a type-check against Helix's real source; lint only in rounds before 2026-10-14), and the problems go back to it to fix (up to 2 rounds).

levels.label: full repo
levels.detail: Everything together: AGENTS.md and the whole Helix repo
levels.explain: The agent works inside the whole Helix repository: AGENTS.md, contracts, docs and source — the most context it can get.
